claim: MCP Inspector is the transport-agnostic first-stop debugging tool; server logging goes to stderr (stdio) or notifications/message (all transports); covers init/capability/working-dir/env failure modes and Claude Desktop log locations.
quote: MCP Inspector: interactive, transport-agnostic testing UI... This should be your first stop.

claim: stdio servers must log to stderr (captured by host); never stdout; under Streamable HTTP stderr is not captured so use log notifications or HTTP tooling; -32602 occurs when a capability isn't negotiated; absolute paths and explicit env required.
quote: Local MCP servers should not log messages to stdout (standard out), as this will interfere with protocol operation.

claim: Practitioner debugging guide: stdout pollution is the protocol killer (use console.error), prefix logs with server/method/request-id, healthy startup sequence, schema/handshake/timeout/exception failure modes and fixes, mcp dev runs Python under the Inspector.
quote: All diagnostic logs, debug messages, and any non-protocol output must be written to stderr.

claim: Claude Code MCP reference: claude mcp add syntax with -- separator and flag ordering, scopes (local/project/user), /mcp panel shows tool counts and flags empty-tool servers, MCP_TIMEOUT, stdio servers are not auto-reconnected, add-from-claude-desktop import.
quote: All options (--transport, --env, --scope, --header) must come before the server name. The -- (double dash) then separates the server name from the command and arguments.

claim: Inspector is a React web UI (MCPI) plus a Node proxy (MCPP) bridging stdio/SSE/streamable-http; UI port 6274, proxy 6277 (overridable via CLIENT_PORT/SERVER_PORT); proxy uses a random bearer session token, disabled by DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH.
quote: MCP Inspector Client (MCPI): A React-based web UI... MCP Proxy (MCPP): A Node.js server that acts as a protocol bridge.

claim: Official Inspector guide: npx launch commands for npm/PyPI/local servers, the connection/Resources/Prompts/Tools/Notifications panes and what each does, CLI mode with --method/--tool-name/--tool-arg.
quote: Notifications pane: Presents all logs recorded from the server; Shows notifications received from the server.

claim: The Inspector Notifications pane shows JSON-RPC protocol messages, not raw console.log, because on stdio stdout is taken by the protocol.
quote: MCP Inspector only shows the JSON-RPC protocol messages. Can't see console.log output because stdout is taken by the protocol.

claim: Testing a Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint with curl: POST initialize with Content-Type application/json and Accept 'application/json, text/event-stream', capture Mcp-Session-Id, replay it on follow-ups, GET opens an SSE stream, DELETE terminates the session.
quote: Accept: "application/json, text/event-stream" ... All follow-up requests must include the Mcp-Session-Id header with the captured session ID.

claim: JSON-RPC error code breakdown: -32000 connection closed (43% stdout pollution, 28% wrong path), -32001 timeout (~60s), -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal error; unrecognized config fields make clients drop the entry.
quote: stdout pollution (43% of cases) — logs written to stdout corrupt the protocol.

claim: Real-world transport framing bug: server used newline-delimited JSON while the client expected Content-Length framing per the MCP stdio spec, causing handshake failure with 'Parse error: invalid JSON'.
quote: MCP server fails to connect with Claude Code: Content-Length framing vs newline-delimited JSON transport mismatch

claim: VS Code .vscode/mcp.json uses top-level 'servers' key and supports a dev block: dev.watch glob restarts the server on file changes and dev.debug attaches a debugger for Node/Python stdio servers; VS Code restarts the server on config change; logs via MCP: List Servers > Show Output.
quote: watch: A glob pattern, or an array of glob patterns, to watch for file changes that restart the MCP server; debug: Enables debugger setup, currently supporting Node.js and Python stdio servers.

claim: Config schema differs by client: VS Code uses { mcp: { servers: {} } } / 'servers', while Claude Desktop and Cursor use { mcpServers: {} }; this mismatch is a common cross-client breakage.
quote: VS Code: MCP servers need to be configured with the format { "mcp": { "servers": {...} } }; Claude Desktop and Cursor: { "mcpServers": {...} }.
